# Control figure and panel dimensions

[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`figspec`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/)`)`` `[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org)`)`

The **plot panel** is the rectangle in which the data are drawn. Panel
sizing means setting the physical width or height of that rectangle,
rather than only setting the size of the complete image around it.

This matters when several figures will appear together in a paper,
report or presentation. Readers compare the axes and data regions, so
those regions should line up even when one figure has longer labels or a
larger legend.

Two measurements determine the result:

- The **canvas** is the complete image, including labels, legends and
  margins. A call such as `ggsave(width = 85, units = "mm")` sets the
  canvas width.
- The **panel** is the area in which the data are drawn. It receives
  whatever space remains after the axes, labels, legend and margins have
  been placed.

Labels, legends and margins have fixed physical sizes. On canvases of
equal width, a longer label leaves less room for the data. figspec can
instead hold the panel width constant and calculate how much canvas each
figure needs around it.

## See where the space around the panel goes

[`fig_geometry()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_geometry.md)
shows how a figure’s canvas is divided between its data panel and the
material around it. This example uses all 234 observations in
[`ggplot2::mpg`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html), with
its axis text and legend kept at their intended sizes:

Read the diagram from the inside out. The white rectangle is the 62 by
45 mm data panel. The surrounding grey area shows the space required by
everything outside the data:

- The 8.3 mm on the left contains the y-axis tick labels and axis title.
- The 19.6 mm below the panel contains the x-axis text and bottom
  legend, which is why it is the largest allowance.
- The 1.4 mm above and 1.4 mm to the right are mainly outer spacing.

![A diagram showing the measured panel and the space used by labels and
margins on each
side.](data:image/png;base64,)

These measurements turn a vague problem such as “the plot looks cramped”
into a specific choice. Shortening y-axis labels can recover horizontal
room; moving or removing the legend can recover vertical room. If those
elements are needed, figspec shows exactly how much larger the canvas
must be to preserve them.

## Panel-sizing functions at a glance

| What you need | Function |
|----|----|
| Set the overall image size | `fig_save(width = ...)` |
| Set an exact plotting-panel size | [`fig_panel_size()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md) or `fig_save(panel_width = ...)` |
| Find one panel width that fits a complete set | [`fig_panel_width()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md) |
| Inspect the current canvas, panel and surrounding space | [`fig_geometry()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_geometry.md) |
| Check whether a set is aligned | [`submission_check()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/submission_check.md) |

The sections below demonstrate each part of this workflow with real
plots and exported files.

## Keep long labels from shrinking the data area

Both plots below are 85 mm wide and use the same 234 observations,
variables and scales from
[`ggplot2::mpg`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html). The
only difference is the wording of the y-axis tick labels. Because the
longer labels keep their full text size, they take space away from the
rectangle in which the data are drawn.

The pale blue rectangle marks that data panel; the grey outline marks
the complete image. Colour and shape both identify the vehicle drive
type, so the groups remain distinguishable without relying on colour
alone.

`drive_colours`` ``<-`` `[`setNames`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/setNames.html)`(`` `` linewidth ``=`` ``0.6`` `` ``)`` `` ``)`` `` ``figs`` ``<-`` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(`` `` short_labels ``=`` ``base_plot``,`` `` labels_written_out ``=`` ``base_plot`` ``+`` `` The more polished appearance comes from figspec’s
[`theme_spec()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/theme_spec.md),
[`figspec_palette()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/figspec_palette.md)
and
[`figspec_shapes()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/figspec_shapes.md)
helpers. The panel-sizing functions do not recolour or redesign a chart;
they control its physical geometry. This guide uses the styling and
sizing tools together because a finished figure should be both clear and
correctly sized.

### Before: equal canvases, unequal panels

![Two scatter plots with equal 85 millimetre canvases. The plot with
long y-axis labels has a visibly narrower blue data panel than the plot
with numeric
labels.](data:image/png;base64,)

The outer canvases are the same width, but the blue panel on the right
is narrower. Its longer labels occupy 15.4 mm more horizontal space,
leaving less room for the data.

## After: make both data panels the same width

To align a set, first find the widest panel that every figure can share
within the available canvas.
[`fig_panel_width()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md)
measures the space used by each figure’s labels, axes, legend and
margins, then returns the common width that fits them all:

`shared_width`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_width`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md)`(`` `` ``figs``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``"cell_press"``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"single"``,`` `` format ``=`` ``"tiff"`` ``)`` ``shared_width`` ``#> [1] 59.82698`` ``#> attr(,"per_figure")`` ``#> short_labels labels_written_out `` ``#> 75.24028 59.82698`

The per-figure values show how wide each panel could have been on its
own. The smaller value becomes the shared width because it is the only
value that fits both figures.

Apply that width to every plot with
[`fig_panel_size()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md):

`aligned`` ``<-`` `[`lapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/lapply.html)`(``figs``, ``fig_panel_size``, width ``=`` ``shared_width``)`

![The same two scatter plots after alignment. Both blue data panels have
the same measured width. The canvas around the long-label plot is wider
so its labels fit without shrinking the data
panel.](data:image/png;base64,)

The matching blue rectangles show the result: both data panels are now
59.8 mm wide. The second canvas is wider because figspec has added room
for its longer labels instead of shrinking the panel or clipping the
text.

| Figure              | Panel before (mm) | Panel after (mm) | Canvas after (mm) |
|:--------------------|------------------:|-----------------:|------------------:|
| Numeric tick labels |              75.2 |             59.8 |              69.5 |
| Long tick labels    |              59.8 |             59.8 |              85.0 |

The table is the reproducible check behind the illustration. Before
alignment, the panels differ by 15.4 mm. After alignment, both measure
59.8 mm; the outer canvases are allowed to differ so the labels retain
their intended size.

[`submission_check()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/submission_check.md)
measures the same alignment across a complete set:

[`submission_check`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/submission_check.md)`(``aligned``, ``"cell_press"``)`` ``#> `` ``#> ``──`` ``Submission check - Cell Press journals`` ``──────────────────────────────────────`` ``#> 2 figures checked`` ``#> `` ``#> ``!`` short_labels single incomplete (6 recorded requirement(s) not judged)`` ``#> ``!`` labels_written_out single incomplete (6 recorded requirement(s) not judged)`` ``#> `` ``#> ``✔`` Plot areas match across this set (59.8 mm).`` ``#> `` ``#> ``!`` No failures found, but at least one figure is not fully assessed.`` ``#> ``ℹ`` Some requirements are not on record in this specification, so they were not judged.`` ``#> ``Source:`` ``<https://www.cell.com/information-for-authors/figure-guidelines>`` ``#> (verified 2026-08-21)`

Publisher profiles specify the overall image dimensions, not the size of
the plotting area inside the image.
[`submission_check()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/submission_check.md)
therefore reports panel alignment as useful layout information, not as a
journal requirement. Any publisher requirements that cannot be checked
from a live plot remain clearly marked as incomplete.

This workflow is not limited to journals. Replace `journal` and `column`
with an explicit canvas width for a report, thesis, presentation or
dashboard:

`report_panel_width`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_width`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md)`(``figs``, width ``=`` ``150``, units ``=`` ``"mm"``)`` ``report_panel_width`` ``#> [1] 124.8904`` ``#> attr(,"per_figure")`` ``#> short_labels labels_written_out `` ``#> 140.3037 124.8904`

## Set an exact data area

Sometimes the data region itself must be a known size: for example, maps
that will be compared at the same scale, plots that must align in a
report, or a series whose axes should occupy identical space.
[`fig_panel_size()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md)
sets that region directly:

`sized`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_size`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md)`(`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels``,`` `` width ``=`` ``62``,`` `` height ``=`` ``45``,`` `` units ``=`` ``"mm"`` ``)`` `[`fig_geometry`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_geometry.md)`(``sized``)`` ``#> `` ``#> ``──`` ``Figure geometry`` ``─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────`` ``#> canvas 71.7 x 66 mm`` ``#> panel 62 x 45 mm`` ``#> `` ``#> ``Decoration`` - where the rest of the space goes`` ``#> bottom 19.6 mm`` ``#> left 8.3 mm`` ``#> right 1.4 mm`` ``#> top 1.4 mm`` ``#> `` ``#> ``ℹ```  `plot()` this to see it. ``

The data panel is exactly 62 by 45 mm. figspec measures the labels,
legend and margins, then gives the complete figure the additional space
they require. Nothing in the data or scales is stretched to make the
dimensions fit.

## Export files with the same data area

[`fig_save()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)
applies the panel dimensions while it writes the file. This avoids the
usual cycle of exporting, measuring, changing the canvas and exporting
again. Here, two real PNG files are written at 300 dpi. Their labels
differ, but both receive a 62 by 45 mm data panel:

`short_file`` ``<-`` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)`` ``long_file`` ``<-`` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)`` `` ``short_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``short_file``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels`` ``+`` `[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(``title ``=`` ``"Short tick labels"``)``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``62``,`` `` panel_height ``=`` ``45``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`` ``long_saved`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``long_file``,`` `` ``figs``$``labels_written_out`` ``+`` `[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(``title ``=`` ``"Long tick labels"``)``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``62``,`` `` panel_height ``=`` ``45``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`

![The exported short-label PNG with a 62 by 45 millimetre blue data
panel.](data:image/png;base64,)![The
exported long-label PNG with the same 62 by 45 millimetre blue data
panel and a wider surrounding
canvas.](data:image/png;base64,)

| File         | Panel (mm) |    Canvas (mm)    | Resolution |
|:-------------|:----------:|:-----------------:|:----------:|
| Short labels |  62 x 45   | 71.6 mm x 69.9 mm |  300 dpi   |
| Long labels  |  62 x 45   |  87 mm x 69.9 mm  |  300 dpi   |

These values come from the files that were actually written, not from
the code arguments alone:
[`fig_check()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_check.md)
reopened each PNG and read its saved dimensions and resolution. The
panels match. The long-label image has a wider canvas because the text
is preserved at its intended size rather than squeezed or clipped.

For a publication profile, add `journal` and `column`. figspec will
retain the publisher’s required canvas width while fitting the requested
panel inside it:

[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``"figure_1.tiff"``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels``,`` `` spec ``=`` ``"cell_press"``,`` `` column ``=`` ``"single"``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``shared_width`` ``)`

## Use all the available canvas

If a figure must fit an 85 mm space, guessing a conservative panel width
can leave valuable room unused. `panel_width = "max"` measures the
surrounding labels, axes, legend and margins, then gives everything else
to the data panel. The comparison below uses the same plot and the same
85 mm canvas:

`conservative_file`` ``<-`` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)`` ``maximum_file`` ``<-`` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)`` `` ``conservative_panel`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``conservative_file``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels`` ``+`` `[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(``title ``=`` ``"A guessed 55 mm panel"``)``,`` `` width ``=`` ``85``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``55``,`` `` panel_height ``=`` ``42``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`` ``maximum_panel`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` ``maximum_file``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels`` ``+`` `[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(``title ``=`` ``"The widest panel that fits"``)``,`` `` width ``=`` ``85``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``"max"``,`` `` panel_height ``=`` ``42``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`

![An 85 millimetre figure with a conservatively chosen 55 millimetre
data
panel.](data:image/png;base64,)![The
same 85 millimetre figure using the widest data panel that its labels
and legend
allow.](data:image/png;base64,)

| Method              | Canvas width (mm) | Panel width (mm) |
|:--------------------|------------------:|-----------------:|
| Guessed panel width |                85 |             55.0 |
| panel_width = “max” |                85 |             75.3 |

`"max"` is calculated for the particular figure, so it makes full use of
the canvas without clipping its surrounding material. It is ideal for
one figure. To give several different figures a common panel width,
continue to use
[`fig_panel_width()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md)
as shown earlier.

## Setting both canvas and panel dimensions

Canvas width and panel width describe different parts of the same
figure:

    canvas = panel + axes + labels + legend + margins

When you provide both, figspec measures the surrounding material and
checks that the requested combination is possible:

`both_sizes`` ``<-`` `[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels``,`` `` width ``=`` ``120``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``62``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`` `[`fig_geometry`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_geometry.md)`(``both_sizes``)`` ``#> `` ``#> ``──`` ``Figure geometry`` ``─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────`` ``#> canvas 120 x 90 mm`` ``#> panel 62 x 69 mm`` ``#> `` ``#> ``Decoration`` - where the rest of the space goes`` ``#> 9.7 mm across, 21 mm down (sides are not separable for a composition)`` ``#> `` ``#> ``ℹ```  `plot()` this to see it. ``

If the two dimensions cannot coexist, figspec stops before writing the
file. The error states how wide the canvas must be or how small the
panel must become:

[`fig_save`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)`(`` `` `[`tempfile`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html)`(``fileext ``=`` ``".png"``)``,`` `` ``figs``$``short_labels``,`` `` width ``=`` ``65``,`` `` panel_width ``=`` ``62``,`` `` dpi ``=`` ``300`` ``)`` ``#> ``Error```  in `solve_geometry()`: ``` ``#> ``!`` A 65 mm canvas cannot hold a 62 mm panel.`` ``#> ``ℹ`` The axes, legend and margins need 9.7 mm, which leaves 55.3 mm.`` ``#> ``•`` Widen the canvas to 71.7 mm, or`` ``#> ``•```  set `panel_width = 55.3`. ``

## Keep every panel readable in a multi-panel figure

### Faceted plots

Facets multiply the number of data panels inside one canvas. On a narrow
canvas, adding facets can quietly make every panel too small. In this
example, three facets squeezed into an 85 mm canvas leave only about 24
mm for each data panel. Asking for 30 mm panels makes figspec calculate
the wider canvas that the complete figure requires.

`facet_colours`` ``<-`` `[`setNames`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/setNames.html)`(`` `` `[`figspec_palette`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/figspec_palette.md)`(``"okabe_ito"``)``[`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``6``, ``7``, ``4``)``]``,`` `` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"4"``, ``"6"``, ``"8"``)`` ``)`` `` ``faceted`` ``<-`` `[`ggplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggplot.html)`(`[`subset`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/subset.html)`(``ggplot2``::`[`mpg`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/mpg.html)`, ``cyl`` `[`%in%`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/match.html)` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``4``, ``6``, ``8``)``)``,`` `` `[`aes`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/aes.html)`(``displ``, ``hwy``, colour ``=`` `[`factor`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/factor.html)`(``cyl``)``)``)`` ``+`` `` `[`geom_point`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_point.html)`(``alpha ``=`` ``0.72``, size ``=`` ``1.7``)`` ``+`` `` `[`scale_colour_manual`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_manual.html)`(``values ``=`` ``facet_colours``)`` ``+`` `` `[`guides`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/guides.html)`(``colour ``=`` ``"none"``)`` ``+`` `` `[`facet_wrap`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/facet_wrap.html)`(``~`` ``cyl``, nrow ``=`` ``1``)`` ``+`` `` `[`labs`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/labs.html)`(``x ``=`` ``"Engine displacement (litres)"``,`` `` y ``=`` ``"Highway fuel economy"``)`` ``+`` `` `[`theme_spec`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/theme_spec.md)`(``"cell_press"``, base_size ``=`` ``8``)`` ``+`` `` `[`theme`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html)`(`` `` panel.background ``=`` `[`element_rect`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/element.html)`(`` `` fill ``=`` ``"#F3F8FC"``, colour ``=`` ``"#0072B2"``, linewidth ``=`` ``0.7`` `` ``)``,`` `` plot.background ``=`` `[`element_rect`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/element.html)`(`` `` fill ``=`` ``"white"``, colour ``=`` ``"#9AA4AE"``, linewidth ``=`` ``0.6`` `` ``)`` `` ``)`

`faceted_width_before`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_width`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_width.md)`(`` `` `[`list`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html)`(``faceted ``=`` ``faceted``)``, width ``=`` ``85``, units ``=`` ``"mm"`` ``)`` ``faceted_before`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_size`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md)`(`` `` ``faceted``, width ``=`` ``faceted_width_before``, height ``=`` ``42`` ``)`` ``faceted_sized`` ``<-`` `[`fig_panel_size`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_panel_size.md)`(``faceted``, width ``=`` ``30``, height ``=`` ``42``)`

![A before-and-after comparison of a three-facet plot. On the 85
millimetre canvas each panel is 24.1 millimetres wide; after sizing,
every panel is 30 millimetres wide and the canvas expands to
fit.](data:image/png;base64,)

With conventional canvas sizing, R honours the requested 85 mm image
width by leaving only 24.2 mm for each facet. ggplot2 does not provide
an argument for saying that every facet must be 30 mm wide. figspec adds
that control: it keeps every data panel at 30 mm and calculates that the
complete image must be 102.5 mm wide.

The data ranges and text sizes do not change. The added value is
predictable physical space for every facet, so adding more facets does
not silently make each chart too narrow to read.

### Separate plots assembled with patchwork

figspec can measure through a patchwork composition and control the
physical size of every underlying data panel in the finished file. This
makes an assembled figure subject to the same reproducible sizing rules
as a single plot.

Suppose this composition is first exported on a 120 mm canvas. Its two
panels are about 45 mm wide. If a report layout requires each panel to
be 60 mm wide, setting a larger canvas by trial and error does not
guarantee the result. figspec sets the two 60 mm panels directly and
calculates the canvas required for their axes, titles, spacing and
margins.

![A comparison of a two-plot composition at two physical sizes. A 120
millimetre canvas produces panels about 45 millimetres wide; figspec
gives each panel 60 millimetres and calculates the larger canvas
required.](data:image/png;base64,)

The compositions retain the same data, scales and relative arrangement,
so the comparison isolates the change in geometry. Each data panel grows
from 45.5 to 60 mm, and figspec expands the canvas from 120 to 149 mm
without shrinking the labels.

The result can then be passed directly to
[`fig_save()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/fig_save.md)
for export or compared with other figures through
[`submission_check()`](https://dansemakula.github.io/figspec/reference/submission_check.md).
The composition now has known, repeatable panel dimensions rather than
dimensions inferred from whichever canvas happened to be used.
